chapter: Fisher's band and Jack Laine's bands
title: Carnival balls and parades, covering two bands with one trumpet
summary: Brunies played society balls and the five carnival parades; with mule-drawn floats moving slowly, he started one band, ran to start the next and alternated. The music was marches and ragtime marches.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: It's alright, Mrs. Brunish, if you want to say something, dude, you can move up there and you don't have to play.

We used to play at the Outfellas Hall, big balls like the Druids, Masons and all like that, the Fishies Band, you know. Did they play parades too, like carnival? Parades, yeah. Like carnival parades, we used to have five, uh, five, uh, the whole five carnival parades. The other time I was one trumpet player with two bands. And the floats, they used to be led by mules.
Yeah, I remember some of them.

And they used to be slow. So, one of their bands short a trumpet player. No, no trumpet player. So, I used to take one band, start it off. When I get through, I run up, up to the other band, start that band off, and they go to town. And when they stop, I'll drop back to the other band. And I've been doing that for many years. So, I got just over.
What kind of music did they play in the parades then?

Marches and, uh, ragtime marches. They started jazzed them up then too in ragtime. Yeah, that's right. They call them ragtime. No jazz them days. Yes, it's ragtime. And if everybody ceased to love, put that in it.
